From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, sara.kim@solsticeai.com
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 12:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: observed prefix cache drift — initial notification and follow-up

Sara / team — update and next steps.

1) What happened (short): a parameter change to the prefix-cache eviction policy that shipped as part of krl-20261205 reduced the TTL and altered hash reconciliation behavior for small-prefix keys. Under common short-chat workloads (lots of short prefixes), certain request patterns caused more frequent cache evictions and forced fallback expansion that increased per-request tokenization and p95.

2) What we did (mitigation): we rolled back the eviction param across us-west-1 serving nodes at 11:18 PST. Telemetry shows the rate of eviction-related fallbacks dropped to baseline by ~11:42 PST and p95 is trending back down. We posted an incident at https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-12-07-PRX-1234 (status: mitgating -> monitoring).

3) Customer-facing items:
- Short postmortem (timeline + root cause + remediation) due by 2026-12-10 17:00 PST.
- Full internal RCA and change-approval notes to be available 2026-12-15.

4) Ask: Ben, please prepare a short change note explaining why krl-20261205 included the modified eviction param; include rollback instructions and a proposed test to prevent recurrence. Marissa, please finalize the statuspage entry and post now (I’ve approved the draft). Laura, confirm if any Dedicated customers were affected and reach out to their CSMs.

We’ll keep the channel updated. Thanks for flagging early, Sara — we’ll include a tailored impact blurb for Solstice in the postmortem.

Priyom Das
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
